questions.q: Latencies $42, 45, 47, 48, 50, 51, 53, 55, 58, 150$ ms: numpy (linear) gives $Q1 = 47.25$, $Q3 = 54.5$. Which rule flags 150 as an outlier?
options: Both Tukey's $1.5\cdot$IQR rule and the $|z| > 3$ rule
questions.explain: IQR $= 7.25$, so the upper fence is $54.5 + 1.5 \times 7.25 = 65.375$ and 150 is outside. The outlier inflates the SD it is measured against (masking): with $n = 10$, $|z|$ can never exceed $\sqrt{n-1} = 3$.

questions.q: In the dataset above, the 150 ms value is changed to 1000 ms. What happens?
options: Median and IQR change; mean and SD stay the same
All four statistics change by roughly the same factor
Mean and SD grow a lot; median and IQR do not change at all
Nothing changes — it is still the maximum
questions.explain: The value stays the largest, so the sorted positions used by the median and quartiles are untouched. The mean and SD use every value's size, so one point drags them arbitrarily far (breakdown point 0% vs 50% for the median and 25% for the IQR).

questions.q: Using numpy's default linear method, what is the 25th percentile of $[1, 3, 7, 9]$?
questions.explain: Position $h = 1 + (n-1)p = 1 + 3 \times 0.25 = 1.75$, so $Q = x_{(1)} + 0.75\,(x_{(2)} - x_{(1)}) = 1 + 0.75 \times 2 = 2.5$. $1.75$ is the position, not the value; other interpolation methods (e.g. `lower`, `higher`) would give 1 or 3.

questions.q: Why does scikit-learn's `RobustScaler` suit a feature with a few extreme values better than `StandardScaler`?
options: It subtracts the median and divides by the IQR, so the extremes barely change the scale applied to typical points
It deletes every point outside the Tukey fences before scaling
It squeezes all values into the range $[0, 1]$
It makes the feature exactly normally distributed
questions.explain: Median and IQR ignore how extreme the extremes are, so ordinary points keep a sensible spread. `StandardScaler` divides by an SD inflated by the outliers, squashing the typical points together. RobustScaler does not remove outliers — they remain, just scaled.
